arguments.value: Rare Element Resources and Synchron agreed to an IP rights deal tied to a separate investment agreement and option to buy company shares. The company gave the investor a worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use its rare-earth processing patents and technical information during the option period. If the option is not exercised, the license continues but the investor must pay an annual fee and cannot sublicense to third parties; if the option is exercised before the deadline, the license becomes exclusive, perpetual, fully paid up, and may be sublicensed. The company keeps a limited right to use the technology for itself and its affiliates. The investor must keep unpublished technical information confidential, with limited exceptions. The company generally controls patent prosecution but must give notice if it plans to abandon rights so the investor can step in. Improvements made by the company become part of the licensed technology; improvements made by the investor belong to the investor, and jointly made improvements also belong to the investor, with the company getting a limited license back. The company disclaims warranties about accuracy and usefulness of the technical information, but it promises the listed methods and products should not infringe third-party rights and must indemnify the investor for losses from any breach of that promise. The agreement also covers enforcement of patents, assignment restrictions, export controls, term and termination, bankruptcy protections, and a mandatory dispute process involving negotiation, then mediation, then litigation if needed.
